issues.body: `_premium_window` appends every key ending in `-utilization`; it never checks `window not in BASE_WINDOWS`, despite the constant, docstring, comments, and tests all defining that exclusion. Therefore a normal response containing only `5h-utilization` and `7d-utilization` returns one of those windows instead of `None`. The new `[#720] base-only headers declare NO premium window` self-test must fail. In production, every normal opus5 probe with base headers will falsely declare a premium window; with mixed headers, a base window can also win the max-utilization selection and hide the actual premium bucket.
issues.fix_hint: Exclude `5h` and `7d` before adding candidates (for example, require a non-empty window that is not in `BASE_WINDOWS`), then run the complete `account-usage.py --self-test` and preserve the base-only and mixed-window assertions as red tests for this guard.
issues.title: Premium-window detection never excludes the base 5h/7d windows

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Request changes: the new opus5 premium-window classifier does not implement its defining base-window exclusion. As written, ordinary 5h/7d headers are treated as premium buckets, and the newly added self-test deterministically fails on its base-only fixture. This is both a shipped correctness defect and direct evidence that the proposed change is not test-clean.
